pov.mode: close third, past tense, Cael — with ONE limited third-person window (Vastin, one paragraph, three sentences), the series' established device; the window may reveal only what Vastin perceives and knows.
knowledge_boundary: Cael is nineteen; ten + the located anomaly. Party SIX at Thornwater. Lira one-armed.

THE DISCLOSURE: Lira first, at Thornwater's wall at dusk — nothing changed for him at the line, not in the ring, not at the den, not at the stone; his Arbiter has been dark since a Kindling eleven seconds long and the Quiet had nothing to turn off; he used everything inside and it all worked and he does not know why. Her answer is the B1 Ch16 covenant six books on: 'You told me when you knew. You don't know. So you told me that. Keep doing it.' Then: 'It scares you.' / 'Out there I was the thing the system couldn't hold. In there I was the only thing that worked. I don't know which one's worse.' / 'The second one. You're allowed to say so.'

THE CIRCLE, that night, six for the first time (Oryn included by Cael's decision): the fact stated; the four who saw saying what they saw; Karis's five findings on the table; Seln's professional read verbatim: 'They know something turns Paths off. They don't know something doesn't turn off. Yet.'; Oryn's clinical read verbatim: 'My hands stop at that line. Yours don't. I had my hands in you for twenty minutes and I can tell you what I didn't find, which is a Path. That's all I've got. I'm not going to guess past it.' Nobody theorizes a maker; nobody says why; six intelligent people agree they cannot see the fact's edges and decide what to do anyway: the Fallow Ring is one site; Pike said a handful; the carter's map has three circles; the contract was written inside. Karis: 'We find the others. All of them. And we find out whether they're the same.'

THE VASTIN WINDOW — one paragraph, three sentences, limited third person, the only one in the book: a courtesy copy of an edge-territory broker's completed-contract report, forwarded through a registry office that should have no interest in Lowmarch's board, crosses his desk marked 'Fallow Ring: crew returned, instruments not recovered'; he reads it twice — a broker's report from a town on no registry map, on his desk with no routing note — does not know why it reached him, and files, in the register of a man who has never pretended to knowledge he lacks, that he does not know; returns it unannotated. He recognizes NOTHING; no classified index; still inside; writing nothing.

THE LOSABLE MORAL STAKE named: Oryn, alone with Cael, restating her condition: 'You can read people now. At contact. Me, Karis, Seln, anyone whose wrist you're holding. I read people for a living and I ask first, every time, even when they're dying. You will too.' 'Yes.' 'Say it in the log. I've seen what the log does to you.' He writes it in full: 'The reading turned outward. I ask first. Every time. If I ever don't, that's the day I became the instrument.'
Oryn will leave after this chapter to make up her route (she is three days north by Ch17); this chapter may stage her intention to go north in the morning.

purpose: REPAIR RUN. Apply the four verified findings to v3-runs/book-07/drafts/ch16-r1.md as exact replacements (durations to fifteen days; the ferry to eight days ago; Oryn's lateness to seventeen; the Vastin window stripped of 'provincial' and the requesting-officer clause). No other passage changes.

scene_shape.opening_state: Thornwater's wall at dusk; Lira one-armed; the day after Karis's three facts.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Tell her what he knows when he knows it — and then tell all of them — and accept a condition on the newest thing he owns.
scene_shape.opposition: The size of the not-knowing; the fear of which sentence is worse; the temptation the tenth fragment brings (reading people without asking).
scene_shape.turn: Lira at the wall (fixed exchange). The circle of six (fixed reads from Seln and Oryn; Karis's decision line). The Vastin window (three sentences). Oryn's condition and the log line.
scene_shape.choice: Cael includes Oryn in the circle by his decision and nobody's objection; writes the ask-first line in the log as a standing rule.
scene_shape.outcome: The book's second half decided: find the other circles, all of them, and find out whether they're the same.
scene_shape.closing_state: The chapter ENDS ON THE LOG (the previous chapter ended on dialogue), the second pole intellectually: 'Nothing out here reads me. And at a line you can mark with a rock, every Path in this camp stops, and mine doesn't. Karis won't write her hypothesis. I won't write mine. We're going to find the other circles. Pike said nobody goes in twice. Tomorrow makes three.'

must_include: The Lira scene at the wall with the fixed exchange verbatim (the covenant line; 'It scares you.'; the two sentences about which is worse; 'The second one. You're allowed to say so.').

The circle of six that night with the fact stated, the witnesses' accounts, Karis's findings on the table, Seln's read and Oryn's read verbatim, the four data points (one site; a handful; three circles on the carter's map; the contract written inside), Karis's 'We find the others...' verbatim; no theory from anyone.
The Vastin window: one paragraph, three sentences, limited third person, exactly the content in the knowledge boundary; unannotated; he recognizes nothing.
Oryn's condition restated with the fixed lines and Cael's log rule verbatim ('The reading turned outward. I ask first. Every time. If I ever don't, that's the day I became the instrument.').
The chapter ENDS on the second-pole log entry verbatim as given.

prohibited_outcomes: No theory of maker/purpose/age/nature by anyone; no 'Architect'; no claim that the sites read or measure Cael; only observed facts.
Vastin recognizes nothing, locates nothing, writes nothing; no classified index; no Book 8 material.
No fight; no fragment use except the standing rule's statement; no travel yet.

The chapter does not end on dialogue or an image.
No modern idiom; no feeling/growth declarations; tic caps; no metadata.
Do not use the phrase 'at the pitch' (or 'at that pitch') — it is at the book's cap already (10 uses in Chapters 1–4). Vary attribution registers with other means.

allowed: Thornwater's wall at dusk; the common room at night; the six around a table; Vastin's desk in three sentences (registry altitude, a folder, a courtesy stamp); Oryn's manner; Lira one-armed at a wall.
Dialogue in established voices beyond the fixed lines (short).
